content.value_statement: Complex systems and processes are difficult to explain with text alone. This skill selects suitable Mermaid formats and produces readable, styled diagram guidance.
actual_capabilities: Selects suitable Mermaid diagram types for workflows, interactions, data models, timelines, and journeys.
Produces basic and styled diagram versions for the same subject.
Applies consistent labels, colors, and structure to improve readability.
Explains complex Mermaid syntax with concise comments.
Suggests alternative diagram types when several formats fit the request.
Provides rendering, accessibility, export, and validation recommendations.
limitations: It does not render or visually inspect diagrams without a compatible Mermaid environment.
Environment-specific Mermaid versions may not support every diagram type or syntax feature.
Accurate diagrams require complete entities, relationships, steps, or architecture details.
The skill provides guidance and generated syntax, not authoritative system documentation.

use_cases.title: Document Service Interactions
use_cases.description: Create sequence diagrams that show requests, responses, failures, and participating services.

use_cases.title: Map Business Workflows
use_cases.description: Turn process steps and decisions into readable flowcharts for review and training.

use_cases.title: Plan Data Models
use_cases.description: Represent entities, attributes, and relationships in an ERD before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Flowchart
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid flowchart for [process]. Include these steps: [steps]. Show these decisions: [decisions]. Provide basic and styled versions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear process diagram from known steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build an API Sequence
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid sequence diagram for [API interaction]. Include [participants], success responses, validation failures, and timeout behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: An engineer needs to document service communication and failure paths.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Entity Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Mermaid ERD for [domain]. Use these entities: [entities]. Include attributes, cardinalities, optional relationships, and assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A team needs a reviewable data model before database design.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Architecture Views
prompt_templates.prompt: Model [system] in Mermaid using the best primary diagram type. Provide an alternative view, styling, accessibility notes, and rendering validation steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: An architect needs complementary views of a complex system.

output_examples.input: Show the customer password reset process with success and expired-link branches.
output_examples.output: A basic flowchart and a styled version show request, email, token validation, password update, success, and expiration paths.

output_examples.input: Document checkout calls between the browser, order service, payment service, and inventory service.
output_examples.output: A sequence diagram describes participants, request order, successful responses, payment failure, and inventory rejection, followed by rendering guidance.

output_examples.input: Model customers, orders, products, and order items with cardinalities.
output_examples.output: An entity relationship diagram defines the four entities, their key attributes, relationship cardinalities, assumptions, and an alternative class diagram option.

best_practices: Provide complete participants, steps, relationships, and decision outcomes before requesting a diagram.
Keep each diagram focused on one audience and one communication goal.
Render the result with the target Mermaid version and verify labels, layout, and accessibility.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated workflows and architecture details in one crowded diagram.
Do not omit failure paths, relationship cardinalities, or assumptions that affect interpretation.
Do not accept generated syntax without rendering it in the target environment.

faq.question: Which Mermaid diagram types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It covers flowcharts, sequence, class, state, ERD, Gantt, pie, Git graph, journey, quadrant, and timeline diagrams.

faq.question: Can it choose the best diagram type?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the audience, goal, and source information so it can select and explain a suitable format.

faq.question: Does it provide styled diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill requests both basic and styled versions with consistent colors, labels, and structure.

faq.question: Can it verify that a diagram renders?
faq.answer: It can provide validation steps, but actual verification requires a compatible Mermaid renderer in the working environment.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing Mermaid diagram?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply the current diagram, rendering errors, target Mermaid version, and desired readability or styling changes.

faq.question: Does it support accessibility guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It can recommend descriptive labels, readable contrast, concise structure, and supporting text for users who cannot inspect the diagram.
